children: , the commerce and cloud-infrastructure giant, blocked Meta's (META) Muse AI agent from completing purchases on its marketplace, drawing a clear boundary around who gets to transact inside Amazon's ecosystem. Shares gained approximately 0.8% to $255.83, based on the latest quoted price.

Muse users were told that access through an unauthorized agent violated Amazon's conditions. Meta, meanwhile, says Muse requires user approval before making purchases, cannot access stored payment credentials and relies on one-time cards through Stripe's Link. The clash is bigger than a technical restriction: AI agents are starting to sit between shoppers and marketplaces, putting control of customer relationships, transaction flows and valuable commerce data directly in play.

Amazon's North American business generated $116.2 billion in second-quarter sales and $9.1 billion in operating income, giving the company plenty of economic incentive to protect that relationship. The valuation picture adds another wrinkle: the shares at $255.83 sit 2.74% above the $249.00 GF Value, suggesting the market price is already modestly ahead of GuruFocus' estimate of fair value. For investors, the key question is whether Amazon ultimately treats third-party shopping agents as incremental distributionor keeps the gates closed to preserve control over one of its most valuable assets: the customer checkout.

title: Amazon Gains While Closing Its Store to Muse
